questions.title: Planning an experiment — spring compression by a falling ball

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer:
Diagram: a sheet of cardboard supported by four springs standing on the bench; a rule (ruler) clamped vertically to a stand next to the cardboard to measure the compression c; a steel ball released from a fixed height h above the cardboard, e.g. held by an electromagnet (or at a fixed release point between the springs).
Procedure and measurements: vary r (independent variable) using steel balls of different radii and measure c (dependent variable); measure the initial height of the cardboard/springs and the height when the ball is on the cardboard, so that c = original height − new height; measure r with a micrometer or calipers — measure the diameter d and calculate r = d/2; measure the height h through which the ball falls with the rule and determine v from v² = 2gh; use a range of at least 5–6 different radii; repeat the measurement of c for the same ball (same r) and take the mean.
Analysis: plot a graph of 1/c² against 1/r³ (or 1/r³ against 1/c²). For the plot of 1/c² (y) against 1/r³ (x): gradient = v²/(απρ), so α = v²/(πρ × gradient); y-intercept = Z/v², so Z = y-intercept × v². The relationship is valid if a straight line is obtained (with y-intercept = Z/v²).
Controls: keep v constant — release the ball from the same height each time (fixed release point/electromagnet); ensure the ball hits the centre of the cardboard and use springs each with the same spring constant, so that c is the same for all springs; measure the mass m of each ball with a balance to verify ρ, using ρ = m/(4/3πr³) or ρ = 6m/(πd³); keep the rule vertical using a plumb line or set square, and measure from the bottom of the ball to the top of the cardboard for accurate h and c.
Safety: place screens around the apparatus or cushions/a sand tray on the bench to stop the ball leaving the bench; use springs with a small spring constant or a larger drop height so that c is large enough to measure accurately (or use video with slow-motion playback, with the rule in view, to read the minimum height).

questions.title: Oscillating steel strip — period, width & Young modulus

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer:
E = 16π²ML³/(wT²d³), so T² = (16π²ML³/(Ed³)) × (1/w)
Comparing with y = mx: gradient = 16π²ML³/(Ed³)

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer:
All six points from (b) plotted correctly — each within half a small square of its true position, with point diameter less than half a small square (check the second and fifth plots from the left; ecf from 2(b)).
Error bars in T² plotted for all six points — total length of each bar accurate to less than half a small square and symmetrical about the point.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.answer:
Straight line of best fit drawn (not from the top point to the bottom point; line thickness less than half a small square; must pass between (65.0, 0.090) and (67.0, 0.090) and between (103.0, 0.140) and (104.0, 0.140)).
Worst acceptable line drawn — the steepest or shallowest line that passes through all the error bars (may be constrained by an intermediate error bar).
Label both lines.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.answer:
Using two widely spaced points on the best-fit line (Δx at least 35), with clear substitution into Δy/Δx:
gradient = (0.160 − 0.0734)/(118 − 52.1) = 0.0866/65.9 = 0.0013 (expect about 0.0011 − 0.0015)
Absolute uncertainty = gradient(best fit) − gradient(worst acceptable line), or ½(steepest gradient − shallowest gradient) = ± 0.0001
gradient = 0.0013 ± 0.0001 s² m

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.answer:
E = 16π²ML³/(gradient × d³) = 16π² × 0.100 × 0.262³/(0.00131 × (9.7 × 10⁻⁴)³)
= 0.284/(0.00131 × 9.13 × 10⁻¹⁰) = 2.4 × 10¹¹ N m⁻² (expect about 2.4 × 10¹¹; 2–3 s.f.; ecf from 2(c)(iii) and 2(d))
Unit of E: N m⁻² or Pa (kg m⁻¹ s⁻²)

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.answer:
%unc(E) = (ΔM/M + 3ΔL/L + 3Δd/d + Δgradient/gradient) × 100%
= (5/100 + 3 × 0.2/26.2 + 3 × 0.03/0.97 + 0.0001/0.00131) × 100%
= 5% + 2.3% + 9.3% + 7.6% = 24% (must be greater than 7%; with the correct Δd from 2(d) alone, at least about 16%; max/min method allowed)

parts.label: (f)
parts.answer:
T² = gradient × (1/w), so w = gradient/T²
w = 0.00131/0.500² = 0.00131/0.250 = 5.2 × 10⁻³ m (expect about 5 × 10⁻³; minimum 2 s.f.; ecf from 2(c)(iii) and 2(e)(i))
Δw/w = 2 × ΔT/T + Δgradient/gradient = 2 × 0.004/0.500 + 0.0001/0.00131 = 0.016 + 0.076 = 0.092
Δw = 0.092 × 5.2 × 10⁻³ = 4.8 × 10⁻⁴ m
w = (5.2 ± 0.5) × 10⁻³ m (max/min method allowed; or using E and d with Δw/w = ΔM/M + 3ΔL/L + 3Δd/d + ΔE/E + 2ΔT/T)
